text:
alex: FYI seeing a sharp 99th latency spike (~2.1s) during yesterday's customer burst. Suspect warm-pool fork fairness issue + KV warmup thrash. Traces attached.

maria: Which cluster/region and timeframe? can you paste logs or a trace id?

alex: us-west-2, ~18:22-18:27 UTC. Quick log excerpt from the runtime profiler:
```
WARN kernel-selection: fallback=generic-kernel reason=fork_hotpath_mismatch latency_ms=2103 probe_id=pf-892
PROF kv-cache: miss_rate=0.72 warmup_seconds=12.4 prefetch_items=384
ALLOC warm-pool: forked_worker_id=fw-33 hold_time_ms=12400
```
flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/1925012345 (private)

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-1221 created: autoscale lag / warm-pool fairness. Pages sent to oncall.

jon: We shipped a change to kernel heuristics last week to prefer forked workers for coldstart avoidance. Could be starving capacity if forks hold GPUs longer due to KV prefetch. Noted similar signal in canary metrics.

sam: dug into allocation logs — warm forks are prefetching full KV sets at creation. That prefetch path triggers a heavy kernel on certain models which pins GPU memory longer. When two bursts overlap, one fork hogs the queue and others wait -> alloc queue grows -> provisioning lag -> latency spike (noisy neighbor effect).

maria: Immediate mitigation: disable fork allocation on a small canary in us-west-2 to force unified pool allocation and avoid the aggressive prefetch path.
Command to patch canary:
```
redwoodctl patch cluster us-west-2 --set runtime.feature.fork_allocation=false --env canary
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: rollout_id=r1234 -> runtime.feature.fork_allocation=false. Observability dashboards: https://console.internal/d/rollouts/r1234

alex: After canary (~5m post-change) p99 dropped from ~2.1s to ~420ms, throughput stable. Queue depth normalized. Thanks.

jon: Root cause hypothesis: new batching heuristics triggered aggressive KV prefetch at fork creation. That prefetch ramps up expensive kernel selection paths (larger sequence lengths -> different kernel) and holds GPU for longer. Combined with tightened kernel-fallback thresholds, we ended up with more cache misses and longer warm paths. Need to throttle prefetch and adjust kernel selection thresholds.

maria: Action items:
- revert fork_allocation=false in prod until heuristics are adjusted (ops)
- add synthetic replay that simulates overlapping bursts to catch warm-fork fairness regressions (eng-runtime)
- expose kv_prefetch_time and fork_hold_time as alerts (observability)
- follow-up ticket: INC-2026-1221 (owner: sam)

sam: I'll open a PR with a conservative kv-prefetch cap (default 64 items) + unit test that simulates warm-fork prefetch under concurrent bursts. tagging @jon for review.

alex: Can someone also add a perf test that runs kernel-selection profiler during warm-fork startup? We need a baseline flamegraph pre/post heuristic tweak.

jon: Yep, adding a perf job to the CI perf suite. Will include kernel-selector flamegraph and kv cache heatmap outputs.

maria: Marking the immediate incident as mitigated in the timeline. Please add all artifacts to INC-2026-1221 and include links to PRs and flamegraphs.

alex: Great work everyone. Keep monitoring for the next 24h and report any regressions. :thumbsup:
